function: FDD downlink beamforming: user encoders compress estimated channels for feedback; BS decoder outputs beamformers, refined by gradient ascent; hybrid digital beamformer too (p. 2, p. 5, p. 12).
system: Sparse mmWave channel, BS with N=64 antennas; MISO K=16 single-antenna users; MIMO K=4 users with M=4 antennas; near-field hybrid, wavelength 3 mm; no RIS (p. 4, 8, 15).
method: Semi-amortized encoder-decoder: FC encoder, beamformer decoder, channel decoder; gradient ascent steps inside training; two-phase training with LMMSE knowledge distillation, supervised to unsupervised (p. 5-7).
data_channel: Custom sparse geometric mmWave channel with L=10 paths and 0.1 rad angular spread, randomly generated; near-field piecewise-far-field model; no standard or measured data (p. 4, 6, 8, 15).
test_conditions: Trained over SNR 5-20 dB, tested across SNRs; user number K and channel-error variance swept in Fig. 9; no train-test mismatch in K or error stated (p. 10-11).
baselines: Learned: DNN [15], WMMSE-guided DNN [17], CRGAT GNN [34], IAIDNN unfolding [32], EDN and unsupervised-only ablations; non-learned: WMMSE [4], LMMSE (p. 9-11).
metrics: Average sum rate versus SNR, user number and channel-error variance; training convergence curves; average CPU inference time (p. 8-12).
complexity: Inference complexity O(KMN(hG+hF+hJ)+K^2 N Qi), Eq. 19; CPU time 7.86 ms versus WMMSE 4.84 s and IAIDNN 112.34 ms, Table 1 (p. 11-12).
q1_support: p. 4: "we consider a geometric channel model with L scattering paths"; a custom sparse mmWave simulator, with no 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO or measured channel.
q2_support: p. 10: "The trained models are then evaluated across a range of SNR values" (an SNR sweep); Fig. 9 sweeps K and channel error without stating that a model trained at one value is tested at another; p. 16 leaves "generalizability to varying problem configurations" as future work.
q3_support: p. 10: "WMMSE [4]: The original WMMSE algorithm" (non-learned) and "DNN [15]: A DNN model tailored to the beamforming" (learned); "the proposed SA-EDN scheme consistently outperforms all baselines under imperfect CSI" in sum rate (Fig. 9).
q4_support: p. 11: "we also report the average CPU inference time of all schemes in Table 1"; Eq. 19 gives the inference complexity order O(KMN(hG+hF+hJ)+K^2 N Qi).
q5_support: p. 8: "channel samples are generated according to the sparse channel model"; simulated data only, and the paper gives no link to code or data.
notes: Include, area 3: sum-rate beamforming is the main metric, while the encoder compresses the channel for feedback. q2 is 0: p. 3 claims generalization across settings, but the evidence is an SNR sweep and K and CSI-error sweeps, the decoder input and output sizes depend on K (p. 6), and no unseen setting is stated. Fig. 10 (p. 12) trains with Gaussian feedback error and checks against the real feedback process, which is not a new scenario.
